svg.text: Peer-to-Peer Distributed Storage, Merkle DAG, Bitswap Protocol, Kademlia DHT & Blockchain Pinning

g.text: 1. LOCATION ADDRESSING (HTTP) vs. CONTENT ADDRESSING (IPFS CID)
• Vulnerable: If university domain expires, server moves, or admin alters file, link breaks or serves tampered data.
• Cryptographic Guarantee: Address is derived directly from cryptographic hash of the content.
• Anyone who modifies 1 character generates a completely different CID. Retrievable from ANY peer.
★ Self-describing standards ensure future-proof algorithmic upgrades without breaking references.
• Files larger than 256 KB are split into 256 KB raw chunks.
• Each chunk is hashed into a leaf node, and organized into a UnixFS Merkle DAG tree.
★ Result: Root CID mathematically represents the ENTIRE document structure.
If only Chunk 4 changes, only 110 KB is re-uploaded; Chunks 1-3 are reused across the entire network.
• Answers two fundamental questions: "Who has CID X?" and "Where is Peer Y?"
• Routing table with XOR distance metric organizes peers into k-buckets (O(log N) lookup).
• Nodes maintain a "Wantlist" (blocks desired) and a credit/debit ledger with peers.
• Tit-for-Tat game theory prevents freeriding and rewards nodes that contribute bandwidth.
3. Bitswap Wantlist Sent directly to Provider Node
4. Raw Block Data Streamed & Recalculated locally
• IPFS does NOT guarantee perpetual storage by itself. Unpinned files are pruned during
routine Garbage Collection (GC) when node disk thresholds are reached.
★ "Someone must PIN the content to guarantee 24/7 availability."
struct Document { address issuer; string ipfsCID; uint256 timestamp; }
• Smart contract retains immutable audit proof and cryptographic signature.
• IPFS network distributes heavy document payloads freely at zero gas cost!
